newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down on Thursday on profit-taking after technical corrections over the past few days, traders said.
The key November contract ended at 3,295 yuan ($396) per tonne, down 15 yuan. It opened at 3,313 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 3,315 and a low of 3,286.
January fell four yuan to 3,226 yuan, March five to 3,235 and May seven to 3,310.
Combined volume fell to 17,400 tonnes from 19,200.
Traders said long and short position holders liquidated their positions because of an unclear short-term trend.
"Liquidation by retail investors dominated today's trading," one trader said.
Traders said that there was an over-supply of spot soybean and lower spot prices will limit potential rises of futures contracts. The price of spot soybean is around 3,300 yuan per tonne in Shanghai.
"It is hard to hold futures prices above that level without market-moving news," a second trader said.
